entries.clue: Smear of clay, dung and straw packed over woven staves to close a wall
Derbyshire town that lent its name to a jam and almond tart
Milled from the entire grain, bran and all: the brown bread
Shortened name for the flooring made from linseed oil and cork
Twenty-pence piece and the like, fed in to start the drum
Flat metal sheet on which biscuits are spaced out before going in the oven
Enclosed yard inside the outer wall, holding stables, forge and storehouses
Heavy flanged club, swung from the saddle to crush what a blade could not cut
Stale and mouldy in odour, as wet things left overnight go
Frothy white bubbles climbing the glass door as the wash gets going
Officer who cried the proclamations and knew every noble family's arms
